NFL DFS Wide Receiver Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 24, 5:01 PM ET

Ja'Marr Chase is the top-projected wide receiver on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 23.4 DraftKings points for $8,900, against New Orleans. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (20.9, $9,100) and Justin Jefferson (17.5, $7,800) are next.

Ja'Marr Chase is also the top value at the position: 2.63 projected points per $1,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 24, 5:01 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Wide receivers to know in Week 12

Ja'Marr Chase, CIN vs NO ($8,900)

Ja'Marr Chase carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 23.4 DraftKings points at $8,900, the 2nd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 2.5 points clear of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The model gives him 9.2 targets on 35.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.63 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 20 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Chase averaged 23.5 points with a simulated floor of 9.7 and a ceiling of 48.9, and he holds 31% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cincinnati is a 10-point favorite at home against New Orleans, with an implied team total of 30.25 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, SEA at SF ($9,100)

Jaxon Smith-Njigba projects 2nd at the position with 20.9 DraftKings points at $9,100, 5th on the main slate overall. The model gives him 9.0 targets on 25.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.30 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 20 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Smith-Njigba averaged 20.9 points with a simulated floor of 7.5 and a ceiling of 46.6, and he holds 16% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Seattle is a 3-point underdog on the road against San Francisco, with an implied team total of 21.75 in a game totaled at 46.5.

Justin Jefferson, MIN vs ATL ($7,800)

Justin Jefferson projects 3rd at the position with 17.5 DraftKings points at $7,800. The model gives him 8.1 targets on 26.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.25 projected points per $1,000, 10th of 20 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Jefferson averaged 17.5 points with a simulated floor of 4.7 and a ceiling of 42.7, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Minnesota is a 7-point favorite at home against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 24.25 in a game totaled at 41.5.

Value: Caleb Douglas, MIA vs NYJ ($4,500)

Caleb Douglas projects for 11.8 DraftKings points at $4,500, which works out to 2.62 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 20 wide receivers the model projects for 9 or more points. The model gives him 6.0 targets on 23.1 routes. Across 50,000 simulations Douglas averaged 11.8 points with a simulated floor of 3.8 and a ceiling of 26.9, and he holds 14% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 3.5-point underdog at home against the Jets, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 40.5.
